record.paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
record.original_question: For an electron modeled as an extended structure with intrinsic properties rather than as a spinning top or modified point particle, which intrinsic property or combination of intrinsic properties is actually related to electric charge?

evidence.quote:
Returning to Barut’s dilemma quoted in the introduc-
tion, it can be said that in this model the electron is nei-
ther a spinning top nor any modiﬁed point particle: it is
an extended structure, and so far it is not clear, which of
the intrinsic properties of the electron is actually related
to its charge.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Model the electron not as a point particle nor as a classical spinning top, but as a spatially extended structure characterized by a collection of intrinsic properties (such as mass, spin, magnetic moment, internal frequency/zitterbewegung, internal geometric or topological invariants, and similar features). Identify which single intrinsic property, or which specific combination of intrinsic properties, of such an extended electron structure should be identified as the physical origin of its electric charge. In other words, give a precise mathematical correspondence expressing the electric charge e of the electron in terms of these intrinsic properties.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive derivation of electric charge from intrinsic properties of an extended electron model is established in the literature; the question of the geometric/dynamical origin of electric charge remains an open problem in foundations of physics, with various proposals (zitterbewegung, topological soliton charges, Kerr–Newman-type geometries) but no accepted answer.

status_evidence.claim: The identification of which intrinsic property corresponds to electric charge in extended electron models is unresolved.
